text.p: Moldovan President Petru Lucinschi on Tuesday dismissed Privatisation Minister Ceslav Ciobanu and replaced him with Iurie Badir, a member of the state audit office, the president's press service said.
The presidential decree gave no reason for the dismissal. Ciobanu had offered his resignation last month. He denied an accusation of corruption levelled at him by a parliamentary committee.

Earlier this month, the parliament had expressed a vote of no confidence in Ciobanu, based on the committee's allegations that he had favoured the illegal sale by the state of a sanatorium to a company whose founders included his wife.
Parliament had requested the president and the prime minister dismiss Cionbanu, who submitted his resignation to the prime minister two weeks ago, while denying the charges.
"Parliament's accusation is not objective," Ciobanu told a news conference on Tuesday, two hours before the president's decree accepting his resignation was made public.
In turn, Ciobanu accused parliament of impeding the adoption of the 1997-1998 privatisation programme, which he said could therefore threaten a $35-million World Bank loan.
